clue.text: Unfashionable item of jewellery linked to ears all over the place

indicators.note: unfashionable is 'not in', so the word in is taken out of the jewellery item

parts.note: a chain is a piece of jewellery worn round the neck
in means fashionable, the letters removed
otic is the anatomical adjective meaning relating to the ears

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a dated earring arrangement that dangles everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IN (fashionable) out of CHAIN to leave CHA, then add OTIC, the medical word for 'of the ear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chaotic is in total disorder, scattered with no plan, which is what all over the place describes.

clue.text: Fourth line of pews installed in church before day gets busy

indicators.note: before says the church piece comes ahead of the day letter
installed in says the row goes inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a row is a line of seats such as pews
D is the fourth letter, so the fourth row is row D

explanation.surface: A church fills up as people take the fourth row of pews before the day's service.
explanation.walkthrough: Rows of seating are lettered, so the fourth line is row D.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowded place is packed with people, which is one sense of a busy place.

clue.text: Loyalist essentially fibbing and joining forces

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of the word, its middle two letters

parts.note: middle letters of loyalist
fibbing means telling lies

explanation.surface: A loyalist who lies at heart teams up with others.
explanation.definitionFit: Allying is uniting with another party for a shared purpose, as nations do in an alliance.

clue.text: Wrong base for dessert

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A cook has used the wrong pastry base for a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a legal wrong; E is the mathematical constant used as the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich layered cake served as a sweet course.

clue.text: Silicone breast — perhaps one dropping halfway down — firm at first, becoming flexible

indicators.note: at first says the firm comes at the start

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: dropping halfway down says the one leaves the front and falls to the middle of the word

parts.note: a silicone breast is an example of an implant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cosmetic surgery tale of a silicone breast sagging, firm at first but softening later.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as surgery gossip, but 'one dropping halfway down' is an instruction: the letter for one falls from the front of the implant word to its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Compliant means yielding or accommodating, the sense in which a person or material is flexible.

clue.text: Pump gallons before turning over my small garden

indicators.note: before says the gallons letter comes ahead of the rest
turning over says the word my is read backwards

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to garden can mean to hoe, working the soil with a tool

explanation.surface: Someone pumps fuel before turning to tend their little garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pump' looks like a verb about fuel, but it is the noun: a light canvas shoe worn for gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A pump is a light plimsoll-style shoe, the kind worn for physical education lessons.

clue.text: Understood the woman's withdrawn in confinement

indicators.note: withdrawn says those letters are taken out

parts.note: gathered means understood, as in 'I gathered as much'
her refers to the woman

explanation.surface: A woman is understood to have withdrawn while confined.
explanation.walkthrough: Gated is a British school and university punishment: being confined to the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A gated student is restricted to college grounds, a form of being kept in confinement.

clue.text: First man infiltrating a group of spies after Bond's boss is hard nut to crack

indicators.note: after says these letters follow the boss

parts.note: M is James Bond's boss in the Fleming novels

indicators.note: infiltrating says the first man gets inside the spies

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
Adam was the first man in the Bible

explanation.surface: An agent infiltrates a spy ring under orders from M, a tough case to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard nut to crack' sounds like a difficult person; the nut is literal, with a famously hard shell.
explanation.definitionFit: The macadamia is an Australian nut with an exceptionally tough shell that needs special crackers.

clue.text: Idiot putting drink on card

indicators.note: on in a down clue says the drink sits above the card

parts.note: a half is a half-pint of beer
a card is a joker or wag, a wit

explanation.surface: A fool puts his drink on a playing card at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: A card is an amusing, eccentric person, as in 'he's a real card'.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfwit is a foolish or stupid person, someone seemingly lacking a full set of wits.

clue.text: Notice French city near the start

parts.note: ear means attention or notice, as in 'give ear to'
Lyon is a city in France

explanation.surface: A notice tells travellers about a French city nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Early on means at an initial stage, close to the beginning of something.

clue.text: Painting house — one with crude interior?

parts.note: an oil is a painting done in oil paints
drum is slang for a house or home

explanation.surface: An art critic describes a painting of a house with a vulgar interior.
explanation.walkthrough: Drum is slang for a house or flat. 'Crude' reads as vulgar, but it is crude oil, which fills the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A large metal barrel used to store petroleum holds crude inside it, hence the whimsical question-mark description.

clue.text: Heart in mouth for loser — quite the reverse for poker

indicators.note: in, with the following 'quite the reverse', says the heart word holds the other piece rather than going inside it
quite the reverse swaps the roles of container and contents named just before

parts.note: ticker is slang for the heart

indicators.note: the mouth of a word is its opening, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: first letter of loser

explanation.surface: A card player's heart is in their mouth when losing a poker hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally it says put TICKER in L; 'quite the reverse' says put L inside TICKER instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A tickler is an old name for a fire poker, the rod used to stir up coals in a grate.

clue.text: Data storage device computer manufacturer rejected made little sense

parts.note: a drive, such as a hard drive, stores computer data

indicators.note: rejected says the maker's name is turned back to front

parts.note: Dell is an American computer maker

explanation.surface: A hard drive that a PC firm turned down produced gibberish.
explanation.definitionFit: To drivel is to talk nonsense, so someone who did so spoke without making much sense.

clue.text: Provide with Railway Union fund

parts.note: do can mean provide, as in 'can you do me a sandwich?'

explanation.surface: A railway trade union is asked to contribute to a fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Railway Union' suggests a trade union, but the union is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowry is property or money a bride's family brings to a marriage, a fund for the wedded couple.

clue.text: Follow mother's teaching

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Children are told to obey what their mother teaches them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles laid down by an authority, a doctrine or body of teaching.

clue.text: Industry that could explore Milky Way's chocolate bar range

definitions.text: Industry that could explore Milky Way

parts.note: Aero is a British bubbly chocolate bar
space can mean range or extent, as in a space of time

explanation.surface: A sweet shop shelf holds a Milky Way among a range of chocolate bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Milky Way is also a chocolate bar, which makes it look like part of the wordplay; it is the galaxy.
explanation.definitionFit: The aerospace sector builds aircraft and spacecraft, which might one day travel through our galaxy.

clue.text: Machine putting fruit in precious metal can at last

indicators.note: in says the fruit goes inside the metal symbol and the final letter together

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of can

parts.note: last letter of can
a tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: A machine is canning fruit inside a container made of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a self-operating machine, especially a mechanical figure that moves by itself.

clue.text: Extremely troublesome way to pay Northern Ireland for a European approach

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last

parts.note: first and last letters of troublesome

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one piece is swapped in for the other

parts.note: a cheque is a way of paying
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Paying Northern Ireland by cheque is a troublesome European approach.
explanation.definitionFit: A technique is a method or way of doing something, a particular approach to a task.

clue.text: Hardened sinner's opening religious books penned by priest

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of sinner

indicators.note: penned by says the books are enclosed within the priest

parts.note: a cleric is a member of the clergy, such as a priest
OT is the Old Testament, a set of religious books

explanation.surface: A hardened sinner begins confessing to a priest who holds holy books.
explanation.definitionFit: Sclerotic describes tissue that has become hard, and by extension an institution grown rigid.

clue.text: Colour of garment mostly worn by females

indicators.note: worn by says the females letters are wrapped in the garment
mostly says the garment word loses its final letter

parts.note: a sarong is a wrapped skirt-like garment
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A colourful garment is mostly worn by women.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is a deep orange-yellow hue, named after the spice from crocus flowers.

clue.text: Glossary requires study once mounted digital display unit missing power leads

indicators.note: mounted in a down clue means the letters climb upwards, reading backwards
missing says a letter is taken away

parts.note: a pixel is the smallest unit of a digital display

indicators.note: leads picks the leading letter

parts.note: first letter of power
con is an archaic word for study or learn

explanation.surface: A glossary needs study on screen, where a display unit has lost power.
explanation.walkthrough: PIXEL loses its P to leave IXEL, which reads upwards as LEXI.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is a vocabulary list or dictionary, and a glossary is a list of words with meanings.

clue.text: Bring back some carrot cake and ham?

indicators.note: Bring back says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone returns food: carrot cake and some ham.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'and ham' as the definition; 'and' is only a link word, and 'ham' alone defines the answer. Ham looks like the meat but is an overacting performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is a performer who overacts, so the word for a stage player fits with a question mark.

clue.text: Couples recalling occasionally upbeat dance

parts.note: a couple is two of something, so couples are twos

indicators.note: recalling means calling back, so the picked letters run backwards
occasionally picks every other letter

parts.note: alternate letters of upbeat

explanation.surface: Couples remember now and then the cheerful music of their dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-step is a ballroom dance in march or polka time with sliding steps.

clue.text: What's left of liberation making Conservative papers

indicators.note: making, with 'papers', says the Conservative letter is turned into something else
papers are ID, identity documents, which replace the Conservative letter

parts.note: a rescue is a liberation from danger

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician's leftover policy on liberation is put in papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making Conservative papers' turns the C of RESCUE into ID, identity papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is the remainder of something after the rest has been removed or used.

clue.text: Nine iron's bagged before Woods finally holes

indicators.note: before says this comes ahead of the final letter
bagged says the nine is caught inside the iron symbol

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
IX is nine in Roman numerals

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Woods

parts.note: last letter of Woods

explanation.surface: A golfer bags a nine iron before Tiger Woods holes his putt.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf scene makes 'holes' a verb; it is a plural noun for awkward situations.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixes are tight spots or predicaments, as are holes in the sense of being in trouble.

clue.text: Sailing vessel fine with freight being lead-free, cheap fuel?

parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing ship
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: lead-free says the first letter of the freight word is dropped

parts.note: goods is freight carried by rail or ship

explanation.surface: A sailing ship loaded with cargo runs on cheap unleaded fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuel' and 'lead-free' suggest petrol, but the fuel is food for people.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk foods are cheap, unhealthy snacks, a humorous kind of fuel for the body.

clue.text: Massive sweater dismissing a smelly problem

indicators.note: dismissing says those letters are sent away

parts.note: a jumper is a knitted sweater
per means a, as in 'five pounds a head'
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A huge sweater gets rid of its smell problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper is British for sweater; 'a' here means per, as in a price per item.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo means very large, as in a jumbo jet or a jumbo pack.

clue.text: French setter will flounce

parts.note: the setter is I, and I will contracts to I'll

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman says the setter will storm out in a huff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounce' reads as a verb, storming off, but it is the noun: a ruffled strip on a dress. Setter is the crossword's author, I.
explanation.definitionFit: A frill and a flounce are both ruffled strips of fabric sewn on as trimming.

clue.text: Broadcast miracle save

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A commentator calls a goalkeeper's miracle save on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim is to rescue or recover something, such as land from the sea or waste for reuse.

clue.text: Let out inside pound under cover?

indicators.note: inside says the rearranged letters go into the pound word

parts.note: quid is slang for a pound sterling

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of let are rearranged

explanation.surface: A property is let out for rent, with money changing hands secretly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under cover' suggests secrecy; read literally it is padded with layers, like a quilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Quilted fabric is stitched in padded layers, like a bed covering, so the question mark marks the playful sense.

clue.text: Tyrant taking over New Zealand gets anything but love

indicators.note: taking says the tyrant holds the other letters within him

parts.note: Nero was a tyrannical Roman emperor
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A despot seizes power over New Zealand and grants the people no affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis scoring, so anything but love means any score other than nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Since love is a tennis score of nothing, a quantity that is anything but love is not nothing.

clue.text: Shape of magazine covers press regulator detailed

indicators.note: covers says the magazine name wraps round the other piece

parts.note: Elle is a fashion magazine

indicators.note: detailed means de-tailed, losing the last letter

parts.note: IPSO is the Independent Press Standards Organisation, the UK press regulator

explanation.surface: A magazine's front pages describe the press watchdog in great detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'thorough' but means with its tail removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is an oval geometric figure, a closed curve like a flattened circle.
